notes_for_implementer: This fixture is a real, live production web page (not a hand-crafted test page), captured via in-browser Blob download of the full <body> so all real chrome is preserved: actual cookie-consent banner, actual nav elements, actual footer, actual comment form and newsletter signup widgets. The core question this fixture answers is whether Pith's normalizer can distinguish genuine ARTICLE headings (the 4 numbered/named H2s that structure the actual content) from incidental heading-tagged UI chrome (author bio, newsletter box, promo CTAs, comments, footer topics) that happens to use heading tags for styling reasons unrelated to document structure. A good implementation should either exclude non-article chrome entirely (if it does main-content extraction) or clearly demarcate it as boilerplate/noise rather than blending it into the article's heading outline at the same trust level as genuine section headings. Because this document shares its source article with fixture 10 (irregular-heading-nesting), the heading list above overlaps with fixture 10's -- fixture 07 emphasizes surrounding NOISE (nav/cookie-banner/footer), fixture 10 emphasizes the NESTING IRREGULARITY itself in isolation (just the <article> subtree, no surrounding chrome).
